title: Lumera, a turn based RPG in Godot.
author: RexArtorius
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev! I’ve been a video game fan since 1984, and I’m building LUMERA, an original turn-based fantasy JRPG for Windows, on my own in Godot. 

Lumera brings together what I love about RPGs, a world I want to explore, companions I want to spend time with, and battles that make me think before I act. 

The journey unfolds across seven acts, each with its own Boss. The lakeside campfire in the video shows a quieter part of that journey, where you can rest with your companions before setting out again. I use generative AI to help create environments and character sprites. One of the biggest challenges has been making that artwork feel consistent once it’s in motion and keeping it quick to load in-game. I’ve roughly halved the texture data for some of the largest sprite atlases, and I’m still working on shortening the wait between acts. 

The current build features 74 named enemies, including seven Boss, and more than 60 NPCs.

My latest internal build has passed automated exploration and Boss encounter checks across all seven acts. 

I’d love to hear what you think of this first look.

comments.author: ArtArtArt123456
comments.body:
some feedback: very ai-ish look because of the extreme detail everywhere. but more importantly, the characters look like cutouts because they don't integrate into the surroundings at all. a shadow is the very least that is needed here.

also the BG needs to be a bit more active (animations etc). the parallax needs to be a lot stronger.

replies.author: maxneuds
replies.body:
Hrm for an RPG like that I think it's fine.
I see a bigger problem in creating interesting backgrounds to traverse. An RPG lives from exploration and atmosphere and that's a challenge. Plus story telling of course.

The characters and battle system I think are fine. Nothing special, just the typical but fine. Looking at darkest dungeon for example there are shadows but that's about it.

replies.author: Gustave232
replies.body: I think that the look of the cutouts gives it a certain charm. I agree about the rest though

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body:
Decent start, has vibes of a modernized remake of a very-early-era RPG, which is *not* a bad thing!

I'd recommend giving the backgrounds another pass. They are *way* too busy (because image models work from noise and tend to *include* a lot of it at high base resolutions), and the implied foreground should get a proper parallax effect. For the characters, some depth in placement would help make the game look a little bit less artificial. Just a few thoughts.

comments.author: maxhit_studios
comments.body:
Feedback

Background is equally as detailed as foreground

Sometimes, less is more..

comments.author: NotTerriblyAnonymous
comments.body: I, for one, am very impressed. The spritework is really good, albeit with a few rough edges; what was your workflow? It looks like video>spritesheet to me, which is challenging especially with transitions. And some of the backgrounds I enjoyed, especially the river of gold.

comments.author: KhaosPT
comments.body: Pass your backgrounds with nanobanana and ask it to remove so much details. Also ask it to remove yellow tint. Ask your AI to do a pass at all your sprites and ask it to remove the yellow tint. You also need to animate the backgrounds the character shook like they are walking on an image, at least add some clouds, make something sway, or add differe t parallax levels on the background. Obvious opportunity is the sky moving different to the mountains, make the water reflect or shimmer with some shader, anything to not make it static.

replies.author: KhaosPT
replies.body: To add, I think your logo looks great and the slop comments are coming from the obvious gtp generated backgrounds, get rid of that and I think you have a solid foundation

comments.author: madu_tualang
comments.body: This how you make people stop asking for AI disclosure, you're not hiding anything.

comments.author: RexArtorius
comments.body:
Thanks to everyone who took the time to give feedback, positive or negative. I work on Lumera every day, and this is my first time building a game.

Looking back at the first prototype, I’m amazed at how far it’s come compared with what you see in this trailer. Every day I find something to fix or a part of the game that could work better. Building it solo is hard, even with an AI assistant helping along all the way.

I appreciate hearing what stood out to you, what worked, and what still needs work.

comments.author: Bastisheen92
comments.body: I wouldnt use GPT Image as the model that provides images/backgrounds/assets. Everything this model produces is so oversaturated and sh\*t....had the same issue and my assets looked 1:1 like yours. It ruins the reputation instantly before any gameplay was shown.

comments.author: LiquidZebra
comments.body: I was looking at the first fight, the knight took like 7 hits and didn’t seem to flinch, the impact compared to the lightning intensity is very off

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: Definitely look into adding some shadows to ground your characters. Also, you show a lot of flat and straight corridors, so obviously as you work on the game you’ll have to mix it up and add variety to the level design

comments.author: yo_les_noobs
comments.body: What's your animation workflow? Thanks for sharing
